title: O fim de semana passado — telling and writing a story
title_target: Foi um fim de semana cheio
goal: Bring the whole module together in one skill: telling the story of something that's happened from start to finish, in a clear order — and writing it up in a natural message.
bekal: recognizing the two past forms and knowing which is for events and which for background
linking a story with *primeiro*, *depois*, *no fim*, *por isso*
writing a short message with the right opening and closing

dialogs.title: Diálogo — Contar tudo à dona Fernanda
dialogs.intro: Sunday evening. Budi has just come home, and Dona Fernanda wants to hear everything.

lines.speaker: D. Fernanda:
lines.text: Então, conta lá! Como foi o fim de semana?
lines.id: Come on, tell me! How was the weekend?
lines.literal: so, tell there! how was the end of week?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Foi cheio! Na sexta à noite fomos ao fado, eu e a Ana.
lines.id: It was packed! On Friday night we went to a fado show, Ana and I.
lines.literal: it-was full! on-the Friday at-the night we-went to-the fado, I and the Ana.

lines.speaker: D. Fernanda:
lines.text: E gostaste? A primeira vez é sempre estranha.
lines.id: And did you like it? The first time always feels strange.
lines.literal: and you-liked? the first time is always strange.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: No início não percebi nada. A sala estava escura e havia muita gente.
lines.id: At first I didn't understand a thing. The room was dark and there were lots of people.
lines.literal: at-the start not I-understood nothing. the room was dark and there-was much people.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Depois a fadista começou a cantar e ficou tudo em silêncio. Foi lindo.
lines.id: Then the singer started to sing and everything went silent. It was beautiful.
lines.literal: after the fado-singer began to sing and became all in silence. it-was beautiful.

lines.speaker: D. Fernanda:
lines.text: É sempre assim. E no sábado?
lines.id: It's always like that. And on Saturday?
lines.literal: is always so. and on-the Saturday?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: No sábado dormi até tarde, porque estava cansadíssimo. À tarde fui ao mercado.
lines.id: On Saturday I slept in, because I was exhausted. In the afternoon I went to the market.
lines.literal: on-the Saturday I-slept until late, because I-was most-tired. at-the afternoon I-went to-the market.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Comprei peixe e legumes. Depois cozinhei para os meus colegas.
lines.id: I bought fish and vegetables. Then I cooked for my housemates.
lines.literal: I-bought fish and vegetables. after I-cooked for the my colleagues.

lines.speaker: D. Fernanda:
lines.id: You cooked?! And did it go well?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Correu. No fim ninguém falou português — mas comeram tudo!
lines.id: It did. In the end nobody spoke Portuguese — but they ate everything!
lines.literal: it-ran. at-the end nobody spoke Portuguese — but they-ate everything!

notes: **A sala estava escura, havia muita gente.** Two verbs in a new form: *estava* and *havia*. Both are the other past tense — not for finished actions but for the story's **background**: what things were like, what was around. You don't need to form it yourself yet; just recognize it.

**Conta lá!** — *lá* here doesn't mean "there" at all. It softens the command, making it sound like a warm invitation, roughly "go on, tell me". A very Portuguese structure: *diz lá*, *anda lá*, *vá lá*.

**Ficou tudo em silêncio** — *ficar* again, this time meaning "to become": *ficar em silêncio* (to go quiet), *ficar contente* (to get happy), *ficar cansado* (to get tired). This is *ficar*'s fourth job in this module, after "to be located", "to fit" and "to take (buy)".

**Gente is a singular word meaning "people":** *muita gente* (lots of people); in Brazilian conversation *a gente* even means "we". In Portugal *a gente* is heard too, but it's considered sloppy; use *nós*.
**Correu bem?** — back to the phrase you learned in unit 14. Now you can answer it with a whole story, not just one word.

grammars.title: Two past tenses: events and background
body: Portuguese splits the past in two. One for what **happened**, one for what things **were like**. English blurs this with "was" and "used to", so for now just learn to recognize it — forming it yourself comes at A2.

head: Form
Used for
Example
rows: *A sala estava escura. Havia muita gente.*

after: The five most common *imperfeito* forms, worth recognizing now: **era** (was), **estava** (was / was being), **tinha** (had), **havia** (there was), **queria** (wanted — which you've used since unit 10 as the polite "I'd like").
How to remember it: if you could put "then" or "next" in front of the sentence, it's **perfeito**. If you're painting a picture — weather, mood, feelings, who was there — it's **imperfeito**.
A normal story uses both in turn: *Estava frio* (background) *e por isso ficámos em casa* (event).

grammars.title: Linking a story
body: A good story isn't about perfect verbs but about a clear order. The nine words below are enough for all of A1.
after: **Por isso links cause to effect; porque links effect to cause.** *Estava cansado, **por isso** dormi até tarde* and *Dormi até tarde **porque** estava cansado* say the same thing in reverse order.
*Afinal* is very typical of Portugal and is often used to overturn an expectation: *Afinal não era difícil* = "it turned out it wasn't hard".

grammars.title: Writing a message
body: Portuguese has fairly fixed openings and closings. All you need to choose is how close the relationship is.
after: **Um beijinho** (literally "a little kiss") is the most ordinary way to close a message between friends in Portugal, and it's not romantic at all. Men closing a message to another man use *um abraço*.
In text messages, people in Portugal abbreviate a lot: *bj* for *beijinho*, *abç* for *abraço*, *tb* for *também*, *pq* for *porque*, *qq* for *qualquer*.

sections.title: One whole story, sentence by sentence

blocks.text: This is what a complete weekend story looks like at A1. Notice that there isn't a single complicated sentence in it — what makes it hang together is the linking words.

blocks.title: O meu fim de semana
items: *Na sexta-feira à noite fui ao fado com uma amiga. No início não percebi nada, mas depois gostei muito.*
*No sábado dormi até tarde, porque estava cansado. À tarde fui ao mercado e comprei peixe e legumes.*
*À noite cozinhei para os meus colegas. Correu bem — comeram tudo!*
*No domingo não fiz nada. Li um pouco, vi um filme e deitei-me cedo.*
*Afinal, foi um fim de semana cheio. Para a semana quero descansar mais.*

blocks.text: Read that paragraph out loud three times. Then close this page and tell the story of **your own weekend** with the same structure. If you can do it without stopping more than twice, you've reached the end of A1.

blocks.title: Mensagem para a Ana
items: *Olá, Ana! Tudo bem?*
*Obrigado por sexta-feira. Gostei muito do fado, apesar de não perceber as letras!*
*No sábado cozinhei para os meus colegas. Correu bem, mas demorei quatro horas...*
*Estás livre na quinta? Podemos ir tomar um café ao Chiado.*
*Um beijinho, Budi*

blocks.text: *Apesar de* means "despite" or "even though" and is followed by an infinitive: *apesar de não perceber* (even though I didn't understand). It's a bit beyond A1, but its form never changes — so it's safe to use as one fixed block.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right linking word (primeiro, depois, porque, por isso, no fim, afinal).
items: ____ fui ao mercado, ____ cozinhei.
Dormi até tarde ____ estava cansado.
Estava a chover, ____ ficámos em casa.
____ ninguém falou português.
____ não era difícil!
____ comprei o bilhete, ____ apanhei o comboio.
On Friday night I went to a fado show.
At first I didn't understand a thing.
On Saturday I slept in because I was tired.
In the afternoon I went to the market and bought fish.
In the evening I cooked for my housemates.
In the end they ate everything.

exercises.prompt: Write five sentences about your own weekend. Use one sentence for each of the prompts below.
items: What did you do on Friday night?
What time did you get up on Saturday morning?
Where did you go on Saturday afternoon?
What did you eat on Sunday?
How was your weekend overall?

exercises.prompt: Spaced review — unit 18. Translate into Portuguese without looking back at the unit.
items: What's the weather like?
It's raining.
It's cold in January.
What's the date today?
My birthday is in July.

answers: Primeiro fui ao mercado, depois cozinhei. — porque — por isso — No fim — Afinal — Primeiro comprei o bilhete, depois apanhei o comboio.

Na sexta à noite fui ao fado. — No início não percebi nada. — No sábado dormi até tarde porque estava cansado. — À tarde fui ao mercado e comprei peixe. — À noite cozinhei para os meus colegas. — No fim comeram tudo.
Na sexta à noite fui ao cinema. — No sábado acordei às nove. — À tarde fui ao mercado. — No domingo comi peixe. — Foi um fim de semana muito bom.
Que tempo faz? — Está a chover. — Em janeiro faz frio. — Que dia é hoje? — Faço anos em julho.
